newsitem.title: NIGERIA: 44 killed in Nigerian tribal clash, paper says.
newsitem.headline: 44 killed in Nigerian tribal clash, paper says.

text.p: Forty-four people were killed in a clash between two tribes in oil-producing Delta state, the semi-official Daily Times newspaper reported on Thursday.

There was no independent confirmation of the incident but the paper quoted community leaders in the area as saying it took place last Saturday when Ikpokpo village was attacked by armed men and burnt down.
They said the victims were mostly Ijaw people killed in continuing clashes between rival ethnic groups over the relocation of a local council headquarters.
Last month, armed Ijaw tribesmen occupied oil facilities of the Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group, holding 127 of their Nigerian staff hostages and disrupting oil production by the company.
The hostages were released in batches following delicate negotiations and oil output has since resumed but the atmosphere in the area remains tense.
Clashes have erupted in several other parts of multi-ethnic Nigeria over a recent creation and restructuring of more than 700 local councils.
Government officials have said the action was being reviewed by the federal government in the capital Abuja to correct what one called "glaring anomalies in the exercise."
